Cut v0.0.1-alpha.8: the path-aggregated left-pane tree. Subjects now render as a recursive path trie — split on '/', indented by depth — replacing the fixed Section/Group/Subject model and retiring the telos|atom|bridge|tension|schema whitelist, so agents/handoff/main nests three levels. Leaves show the full path with the prefix faded and the final segment bright; branch nodes read full-weight; the [my work] and [day] section headers are colored. A dual node (subject that is also a path-prefix) appears as both a branch header and a child leaf. is_day_subject now treats the agents/handoff namespace as day vocabulary, so handoff threads sit under [day]. Reviewed by an independent Opus adversarial pass: SHIP (latent findings only, none reachable on real subject names). 56 tests, clippy -D warnings, fmt clean. Tag v0.0.1-alpha.8.

Cut v0.0.1-alpha.9: cospan now renders day's full block vocabulary, and the project gained its first GitHub remote + CI. Two bundles shipped via PR -> green CI -> squash-merge: (#1) day-bridge and day-schema block summaries, closing the gap where alpha.7's design named day-bridge but never implemented it; (#2) robust day-witness rendering — fixes the single-probe bug that rendered {command:"cargo test"} as 'command: ?' by shape-sniffing day's overloaded fence (map vs lone probe) — plus day-docs and day-injection summaries. The cross-repo pass that drove #2 also filed the day-side format inconsistencies as kan-tools/day issues #237/#238/#239. Infra: private repo github.com/maxinelevesque/cospan with GitHub Actions (fmt+clippy+test); the kan signing seed (.kan/seed, in pre-alpha.1 history) was scrubbed with git filter-repo BEFORE the first push and verified absent from the remote — rotation was unnecessary since the repo had never been pushed. 63 tests, clippy -D warnings, fmt clean. Tag v0.0.1-alpha.9.

Cut v0.0.1-alpha.10: the comment gutter view (P1) — telos/comment-roundtrip made visible. The comment sidecar, which already worked headless, is now a fourth TUI view (4/Tab): a picker over files that have a sidecar, and for the selected file its content with an anchored comment gutter showing each comment's live Anchored/Drifted/Unresolvable state (+confidence) as the file changes, with unresolvable comments collected in a resolve-by-hand list. Live re-localization runs via a per-file mtime gate inside the single poll tick (poll-don't-subscribe); read + re-anchor only (writes/threads/reflow/tree-sitter/session-picker deferred). Shipped as PR #3 -> green CI -> squash-merge. Independent Opus review BLOCKED a None-sentinel collision (a deleted source file left the previous file's content on screen and dropped its comments); fixed by tracking the loaded path so a missing source reads empty and its comments become Unresolvable; re-verified SHIP. Human live-TTY eyeball confirmed the render; a follow-up ordered the comment cursor by anchored line so j/k follow the file top-down. 70 tests, clippy -D warnings, fmt clean. Tag v0.0.1-alpha.10.

Cut v0.0.1-alpha.11: comment threads + two display cleanups, shipped as PR #5 and #4 -> green CI -> squash-merge. Comment threads (#5): sidecar comments gain a reply thread and a resolve action — Comment.thread: Vec<Reply> with serde(default) for back-compat; CLI `cospan comment reply <file> <id> <body>` and `cospan comment resolve <file> <id>`; the `comments` list shows a (N replies) [resolved] suffix; the TUI Comments view strip renders the selected comment's full thread (root + attributed indented replies + [resolved]). The view stays read-only/re-anchor-only — authoring is CLI/MCP (observe-now-control-later). Cleanups (#4): short_author now head6…tail4 so signers sharing a key prefix no longer collide (and the … makes the elision honest); markdown block-HTML no longer collapses its lines onto one row. Both features: independent Opus review SHIP, human live-TTY eyeball on the threaded strip. 75 tests, clippy -D warnings, fmt clean. Tag v0.0.1-alpha.11.

Cut v0.0.1-alpha.12: the comment view complete, banking the polish arc before the planned tabs/footer restructure. Shipped via PR #6 and #7 -> green CI -> squash-merge. #6: discoverable comment-view navigation — ←/→ switch files (aliases for [ ]), a per-view key legend in the header (· ←→ file · j/k comment), and ←/→ title hints, after a user found file-switching undiscoverable. #7: the right-anchored comment column with reflow — comments render as compact notes in a right column beside their anchored lines, and a multi-line note pushes the following code lines down (blank rows) so nothing overlaps; pure wrap_text/note_block/reflow_rows, wide-layout only, narrow keeps the single pane, the strip still holds the selected comment's full thread + unresolvable list. Both: independent Opus review SHIP, human live-TTY eyeball. Next, per user vision: a bottom footer/status-bar from `day status-line` (replacing the mis-sourced top day-status panel), then a Process tab (atoms as flowchart + telos drill-down), Ledger (renamed Browser), and Chat (live session buffers — a design discussion). 81 tests, clippy -D warnings, fmt clean. Tag v0.0.1-alpha.12.

Cut v0.0.1-alpha.14: the atom flowchart, shipped via PR #10 -> green CI -> squash-merge. The Process tab's atoms sub-pane is reshaped from a flat list into an ASCII box-and-arrow flowchart: each atom a labelled box laid out in columns by its longest-path depth in the atom DAG (bounded/cycle-safe layout), solid ────▶ arrows on same-row next edges, and the selected box double-bordered. j/k moves the selection; Enter drills into the atom's detail (in/out/next/done/revisits — done/revisits newly captured onto substrate::Atom), Esc returns; a pane switch leaves any drill-down. Back-flows (revisits + off-column/off-row next) are ROUTED as distinct dashed arrows (┄/┆/╰/╯/▲) in stacked lanes below the boxes in single-row layouts (the real DAG), and kept as a ⇢/↻ text list in multi-row layouts where routing would cross boxes (honest-ambiguity). Independent Opus review SHIP twice (base + routing addendum): grid math traced, no reachable panic, self-edge guarded. Human live-TTY eyeball on both. Next per vision: the telos drill-down (statement/witnesses/tensions), then Chat (live session buffers — architecture discussion). 91 tests, clippy -D warnings, fmt clean. Tag v0.0.1-alpha.14.

Cut v0.0.1-alpha.15: the Chat tab, shipped via PR #11 -> green CI -> squash-merge (bb6b729). A read-only cross-harness view of live agent session buffers read from the harnesses own on-disk transcripts (Claude Code JSONL, Codex rollout JSONL, opencode SQLite), scoped to the watched repo and never entering the kan fold. Per-role markdown render with per-harness prompt-tag formatting (registry + code-aware), line-scroll / message-skip / PgUp-PgDn / mouse-wheel / tail-follow navigation with a non-disruptive new-activity dot, and fold groups for back-to-back tool calls and thinking. Codex multi-agent runs split per thread: director vs subagents, guardians omitted, subagents nested collapsibly under their director in the rail. A defined-but-inert WriteChannel seam reserves the P3 control path. 123 tests, clippy -D warnings clean, fmt clean.

Cut v0.0.1-alpha.16: two Process/Chat refinements merged since alpha.15, each shipped via PR -> green CI -> squash-merge. (1) Telos drill-down (PR #12, bb03791): the Process tab's Telos sub-pane becomes a two-column drill-down — a selectable telos list (38%) beside the selected telos's detail (62%) showing its statement (markdown), each witness with its schema/witness probe description, and the tensions naming it with their recorded rationale; Enter/Esc move focus between list and detail, with hanging-indent wrapping. (2) Faded chat date/time labels (PR #13, 70faacd): compact dark-gray recency stamps in the Chat view — last-active per session in the rail (MM-DD HH:MM via substrate::stamp_short) and a per-message timestamp in each header (iso_short over the event ISO ts), UTC and metadata-weight. Both were verified by unit tests (cargo test 130/130), clippy -D warnings clean, fmt clean, real-data smokes, and the operator live-TTY eyeball rather than a fresh adversarial-review atom (the interactive renders are only verifiable in a real terminal). Tag v0.0.1-alpha.16 is annotated + SSH-signed on the release commit; main was two features past the alpha.15 tag before this cut.

Cut v0.0.1-alpha.17: the comment-authoring milestone, complete through the agent-reachable MCP round trip. Two features merged since alpha.16, each via PR -> green CI -> squash-merge. (1) S4 promote-a-comment-to-a-durable-kan-claim (PR #20, 85facbf): a sidecar comment can be promoted to an immutable comment/<file> kan claim carrying the comment id; the sidecar is never mutated (re-promote appends + --cites prior), and the promoted state is read back from the in-memory fold and shown as a diamond indicator. (2) S5 the comment MCP server (PR #21, 964416b): agents read and write the comment layer over an rmcp stdio transport (cospan mcp), backed by a transport-agnostic tool core; a path-traversal guard and plugin packaging (.claude-plugin + .mcp.json + bootstrap hook) landed alongside. telos/comment-roundtrip witness is now MATERIAL. Version bump only in this commit; features shipped on their own PRs.

Cut v0.0.1-alpha.18: the comment-view vision from .dropbox/05-views-ux.md section (2), shipped in two slices each via PR -> green CI -> squash-merge. Slice A (comment-editor-layout, PR #23, ed5649a): the Comments-tab editor-view redesign -- a toggleable file tray (t), the fixed bottom strip removed with its two jobs rehomed (a pinned unresolvable band that stays visible at every width, and the full thread moved to an actionable Enter popup), a full-row comment background band, sticky scrolling for the comment cursor and the new-comment line picker, PgUp/PgDn in the picker, and a dynamically-positioned width-capped compose popup. Slice B (comment-editor-diffs, PR #24, f7edc44): live git working-tree diffs in the code pane -- a new src/diff.rs parses git diff HEAD into current-file-line-indexed added/changed/deletions, rendered as a D-toggleable sign column (+/~) with tints that yield to the comment band and a red gutter-cell highlight framing deletions, shown in all views, recomputed on the poll-and-fold mtime gate. Both slices reviewed BLOCK->fixed->SHIP by independent hostile Opus reviewers and eyeballed by the operator. telos/comment-roundtrip advanced. 192 tests, clippy -D warnings clean, fmt clean.

Cut v0.0.1-alpha.19: mobile Phase 1 — the read-only HTTP/WS API server over the fold (`cospan serve`, PR #25). A localhost HTTP/WebSocket read API: GET /fold, WS /stream (push on refold), GET /comments and /thread (the S5 comment read core). Loopback-only, foreground, no on-disk state, no claim written; the command_bus::WriteChannel seam is untouched. Serves telos/observe-now-control-later; the disposable<->observe-now-control-later tension is held. Merged via green-CI PR #25; independently hostile-reviewed (APPROVE-WITH-FOLLOW-UPS, verified). Follow-ups (symlink guard in the shared S5 core; a /stream connection cap) are localhost-only, deferred to the remote-exposure phase.

Cut v0.0.1-alpha.21: Slice B — `cospan serve` app-level auth + remote-channel hardening (PR #27). A bearer token (minted on by default, in-memory only) gates every route including the /stream WS upgrade, presented as ?token= or Authorization: Bearer, compared constant-time; the embedded page carries its own ?token=. Plus a symlink-resolving path guard (mcp::guard canonicalizes + checks containment) and a --max-stream connection cap (RAII slot release). Stays disposable: no user store, token+counter in memory only, loopback bind and command_bus::WriteChannel untouched. Makes the read channel safe to expose over tailscale serve — the prerequisite for Slice C (writes over the API). Merged via green-CI PR #27; independently hostile-reviewed (APPROVE-WITH-FOLLOW-UPS; no bypass found; a latent empty-token fail-open and a Bearer-precedence footgun fixed in-round with tests). Advances telos/observe-now-control-later.

Cut v0.0.1-alpha.22: Slice A — web view UX pass (PR #28). A Comments tab (files index via the new bare GET /comments endpoint → a file's comments via ?file= → a comment's full thread via /thread), claim drill-in in Browse (tap for full untruncated text, cites resolved through the fold by_cid map, artifacts, author, time — all from /fold), and a resilient /stream (capped-backoff visibility-gated reconnect; render-once startup). Read-only, still one self-contained embedded page (telos/disposable); command_bus::WriteChannel untouched. The bare GET /comments index establishes the resource-collection API shape future views + write verbs extend. Merged via green-CI PR #28; independently hostile-reviewed (APPROVE-WITH-FOLLOW-UPS; no XSS, no path escape/walk cycle in comment_files; one REQ-5 double-render gap fixed in-round). Advances telos/observe-now-control-later.

Cut v0.0.1-alpha.23: Slice C — comment writes over the API (PR #29), the observe->control transition. Opt-in behind --allow-writes: POST /comments (add), POST /thread (reply), POST /resolve, reusing the S5 write cores under a serialized spawn_blocking write lock (no lost updates), auth-gated by Slice B and path-guarded like the reads. Web writes attributed who:"human" id from --author/COSPAN_WEB_AUTHOR (default "web"), server-set and never client-forgeable (cores parameterized as _as; MCP keeps who:"agent"). GET /capabilities reports {writes,author} so the Comments tab shows add/reply/resolve affordances only when enabled. Writes touch only cospan owned .cospan/comments sidecars — no kan claim written, command_bus::WriteChannel untouched; promote-to-kan stays a human TUI action on the laptop holding the seed. Merged via green-CI PR #29; independently hostile-reviewed CLEAN APPROVE (opt-in gate, auth, guard on all three ops, 40 concurrent adds zero lost, unforgeable attribution, no kan/command_bus write, inert write UI — all verified under attack). Advances telos/observe-now-control-later; the disposable tension is recorded and held.

Cut v0.0.1-alpha.24: chat reads over the API (PR #30), the Chat tab — completing the mobile roadmap B->A->C->Chat and the four read tabs (Chat/Comments/Ledger/Process). New src/chat.rs projects transcripts::discover_all/read to JSON: GET /chat lists the repo agent sessions (newest-active first), GET /chat?session= reads one session with every event kind-tagged (message/thinking/toolcall/toolresult/meta) so the client collapses thinking+tool and shows messages. Hand-built allow-list projection that NEVER serializes the session Locator or any local $HOME path; last_active as epoch-millis. get_chat runs under spawn_blocking behind the Slice-B auth middleware; read-only (no chat write, command_bus untouched), extending the resource-collection grammar. The page gains a Chat tab (sessions -> turns, thinking/tool collapse behind a details tap; textContent-only). Merged via green-CI PR #30; independently hostile-reviewed CLEAN APPROVE (no structural path leak — Locator never referenced, verified live against 7 real sessions incl. a 1209-event read; read-only; auth-gated 401; panic-free; XSS-safe). Advances telos/observe-now-control-later; upholds disposable + the no-local-paths-on-the-wire rule + honest-ambiguity.

Cut v0.0.1-alpha.25: mobile file browser + viewer with tap-to-comment (PR #31), closing the on-device comment-creation dead-end. A file with no comments never appeared in the Comments index, so there was no path to add its first comment from the phone. This adds two read-only endpoints -- GET /files (the browsable tracked-union-untracked set via filetree::list, each with a git-status marker) and GET /file?path= (one file's content) -- and a file viewer in the Comments tab, folded behind an all-files|commented toggle (nav stays five tabs). highlight::styled_web projects the existing syntect pipeline to hex so the embedded page needs no client-side highlighter (disposable). mcp::file_view is path-guarded by the same mcp::guard as the comment routes and bounded by BOTH a line cap (FILE_VIEW_MAX_LINES=2000) and a byte cap (FILE_VIEW_MAX_BYTES=512KiB) so a low-newline/minified file is not read whole into memory; UTF-8 decode is multibyte-boundary-safe and binary is rejected. Tap a source line to add the first comment, gated on caps.writes, POSTing the existing opt-in --allow-writes sidecar route (who:human); reads never write a kan claim and command_bus is untouched. Merged via green-CI PR #31; independently cold-Opus hostile-reviewed APPROVE WITH FOLLOW-UPS -- guards/auth/symlink/binary/XSS/truncation all verified against the running binary; finding F1 (line-cap-not-byte-cap memory gap) fixed in-round, F2 (symlink dead rows) and F3 (second comment per line) recorded as follow-ups. 211 unit + 14 integration tests, clippy -D warnings, fmt clean. Serves telos/comment-roundtrip; upholds observe-now-control-later + disposable + kan-is-truth + honest-ambiguity.

Cut v0.0.1-alpha.26: responsive desktop layout for the serve web page (PR #32), the first slice of the web-view UX round. At >=900px the mobile bottom tab bar restyles into a ~180px left nav rail (the same nav element, icon+label), and the list-heavy tabs become master-detail: Comments and Chat each split into a persistent list pane + detail pane, so drilling in opens the detail beside the list instead of replacing the whole view. Below 900px the mobile layout is unchanged. CSS-first: both panes always live in the DOM and a .detail-open class (set on drill-in, cleared on return) drives the mobile one-pane-at-a-time behavior, so there is no JS viewport listener and a resize needs no re-render. The desktop shell is viewport-locked (body height:100vh; overflow:hidden) with the rail, header, content and each pane scrolling independently, so scrolling the detail never drags the rail or list. Now/Teloi/Browse stay single-pane; text/detail columns are width-capped for ultra-wide readability. Page-only change, no endpoint/API change; stays one include_str! document with no new dependency (disposable). Browse master-detail deferred to the browse-content slice (it uses inline expansion, not view replacement). Merged via green-CI PR #32; independently cold-Opus hostile-reviewed APPROVE WITH FOLLOW-UPS -- mobile behaviorally unchanged (specificity cascade traced), .detail-open lifecycle leak-free, /stream+token+render regression-free, no dead containers, no XSS, no new dependency; F1 (detail-column readability cap) fixed in-round, F2 (sticky offset) resolved by the viewport-locked scroll fix after an operator-eyeball scroll bug, F3 recorded. 212 unit + 14 integration tests, clippy -D warnings, fmt clean; operator-eyeballed at both widths. Serves telos/readable-claim-browser; holds disposable.

Cut v0.0.1-alpha.27: teloi drill-down (PR #33), slice 2 of the web-view UX round. The Teloi tab becomes master-detail: the list pane shows tappable telos rows (a full-width .telos-rows stack, chosen over a card grid on operator eyeball) plus the retained "Tensions held" overview, and tapping a telos opens its full detail in the detail pane -- title+statement, each witness shown WITH its probe description from the schema/witness map (an honest "(no probe description recorded)" when absent, honest-ambiguity), the tensions naming it, and the telos's recorded claims rendered with the SHARED Browse claimEl (no second renderer). renderTeloi fills only the list pane and runs on every fold tick, so a /stream re-render never disturbs an open detail; selectedTelos keeps the active row marked; openTelos fills the detail pane and toggles .detail-open. Page-only over the already-served fold (process.teloi/tensions/witnesses, claims["telos/<slug>"]); no endpoint/API change; reuses slice-1's pane machinery; one include_str! document with no new dependency (disposable). Merged via green-CI PR #33; independently cold-Opus hostile-reviewed CLEAN APPROVE (live re-render provably never disturbs an open detail, honest witness fallback, genuine claimEl reuse on correctly-shaped telos-subject claims, slug-matched tension filter, no XSS, no new dependency, honest 2->3 test-count bump). 213 unit + 14 integration tests, clippy -D warnings, fmt clean; operator-eyeballed at both widths. Serves telos/readable-claim-browser and telos/honest-ambiguity.

Cut v0.0.1-alpha.28: Browse rework (PR #34), slice 3 of the web-view UX round. The Browse tab becomes master-detail (finishing the slice-1 deferral): #view-browse is a .view.md with a list pane (a [Subjects | Timeline] toggle + the retained filter + #browse-content) and a detail pane. Subjects mode: grouped subject rows each with a current-state summary (most-recent kind + published/retracted/status badges, all client-derived from the subject's live claims). Timeline mode: every claim flattened newest-first by recorded_at, filterable over subject+kind+summary, capped at 200 with a "showing N of M" note, each a striking per-op row. Per-operation formatting: a KIND_GLYPH map + a .kind color rule for all nine kinds (Subject/Decision/Publication/Plan/Observation/Result/Status/Relation/Retraction). Detail pane: a tapped subject's claims (state header) or a tapped timeline claim's detail, both via the shared Browse claimEl (no second renderer, cites resolved through fold.by_cid). renderBrowse fills only the list content and skips the rebuild when a cheap signature (mode+filter+claim counts+newest recorded_at) is unchanged, so a /stream tick never wipes the list or resets Timeline scroll; desktop panes fill full height (explicit 1fr grid row) and the capped two-pane area (1500px) is centered. The Status VALUE is not in the fold so only a neutral status marker is shown (deferred). Removed the now-dead subject-tree CSS and the unused inline subjectEl/expanded. Page-only over the fold; no endpoint change; one include_str! doc, no new dependency. Merged via green-CI PR #34; independently cold-Opus hostile-reviewed APPROVE WITH FOLLOW-UPS against the real 586-claim fold (live-safe, honest about the un-served Status value, XSS-clean, dependency-free); F1 (dead CSS) + F2 (timeline scroll reset) fixed in-round, F3 (snapshot detail) accepted, plus a follow-up eyeball fixed an id-vs-class specificity bug that had capped the master-detail area at 820px and made the panes fill height + centered the capped area. 214 unit + 14 integration tests, clippy -D warnings, fmt clean; operator-eyeballed. Serves telos/readable-claim-browser and telos/honest-ambiguity.

Cut v0.0.1-alpha.29: Comments file browser folded directory tree (PR #35), slice 4 of the web-view UX round. The Comments tab's All-files mode becomes a collapsible directory tree built client-side (buildFileTree) from the flat GET /files paths: folders are bold, shaded rows with a monochrome inline-SVG folder icon + a ▸/▾ chevron + file count; files are plain rows with a file icon; nesting uses nested containers whose left border draws a per-level depth guide. Starts folded, a session Set remembers expanded dirs, and a non-empty filter shows a flat matching list. The browser excludes kan's .claims/ (and .cospan/) trees (client-side; GET /files still returns them, honest endpoint). F2: GET /files gains an additive `symlink` bool per entry (symlink_metadata on repo.join(path); filetree::list, shared with the TUI, untouched) and the browser badges symlinks [link] and shows "symlinks aren't viewable" on tap instead of the guard error. F3: the file viewer's line number is a distinct add target under --allow-writes (stopPropagation + startAddAt), so a line that already has a comment can take a NEW one; the gutter/code tap still opens the thread. Icons are monochrome inline SVG via currentColor (theme-aware), no dependency added (disposable). Page-side except the additive server field. Merged via green-CI PR #35; independently cold-Opus hostile-reviewed CLEAN APPROVE (tree builder correct, expand state survives /stream ticks since render() never touches Comments, symlinks guarded in both tree and filter modes, no F3 double-add via stopPropagation, endpoint honest curl-confirmed, XSS-clean, filetree::list untouched); nits F-1 (symlink stat on dropped .claims rows), F-2 (file order rides the filetree::list sort contract), F-3 (no collapse-all) recorded non-blocking; two operator eyeballs moved it to the icon+guide idiom then to monochrome SVG icons (from emoji). 215 unit + 15 integration tests, clippy -D warnings, fmt clean; operator-eyeballed. Serves telos/comment-roundtrip and telos/honest-ambiguity.
